summary.intent: Get all open PRs and Entire agent findings (per trail, not just per PR) in the caliper repo addressed and resolved, then keep the speed/fallback-removal work moving.
summary.outcome: Findings on #455, #458 and three rounds on #462 (nine total) were fixed by workers and resolved in Entire with commit and test citations. Main now contains #455, #458, #459, #461 and #463; only #462 and release PR #396 remain open, and a new S7 worker (feat/fallback-off-rows) was started.

repo: Entire findings live per trail, not per PR: use `entire trail finding list <trail#|--branch B> --repo gh/orin-dx/caliper --project gh/orin-dx --freshness any` and grep for IDs starting `01M`.

Findings are resolved with `entire trail finding resolve <id> --branch B --repo ... --project ... -m "Fixed in <sha>: ... test ..."`; Entire does not auto-clear them until it re-reviews, so resolve once the fix is verified in source.
PR bodies are published from files under ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/pr/ via `gh pr edit N --body-file`.
The CLAUDE.md contract says tests should 'fail on base' for behavior changes; the proposed change is to word it by change type (bug fix, output-preserving, feature, concurrency).
Output-preserving perf work is validated by identity diffs against main, the construct lane against the real checker, and determinism gates across thread counts, not by red-green tests.

Storybook live-upgrade (#462) multi-client hazards: open component tracked per browser keyed by channel event sender id; DevServer instance keyed by channel (options.channel ?? options.presets); watches tracked by component and revision; eager sessions share the lazy answer/pending path.

code.finding: Server-wide single 'open' value let two browser tabs clobber each other; fixed in 30fb22ea with per-browser tracking.
Eager (lazy:false) sessions returned early via docgenInfo() and dropped the checker-pending diagnostic, so no upgrade watch started; fixed to use the same pending path.
Empty neighbour list wasn't posted when navigating to the last component, leaving stale prefetch queue; fixed by posting the empty list.
Storybook 11 applyPresets builds a fresh presets wrapper per hook, producing two DevServer instances; fixed by keying the shared instance by channel.
REFERENCE_VERSION needed bumping to 3 for the new pairing rule so version-2 records aren't treated as same reference.
Watcher rejected aliases to gitignored targets; is_source_file now accepts any path discovery reported.

workflow: Passing CLI flags via a shell variable (R="--repo ... --project ...") in zsh passes them as one argument, causing failures and bogus '0 findings' counts; pass flags explicitly.
Subagent hand-backs are not user authority; verify the pushed head, diff the source, and re-check CI before resolving findings.
A failed list command can look like zero findings; sanity-check counts against command output.
Save feedback to memory: resolve findings yourself once the fix is verified, citing commit and test.

friction: Initially looked only at PR-attached findings when the user meant Entire agent findings on trails, requiring correction and a scan of 60 trails.
Shell-variable flag passing broke the first resolve/list attempt and produced misleading zero counts.
An earlier classifier block on resolving findings without explicit instruction delayed resolution.
#462 needed three rounds of findings, all in multi-client and timing edges of the live-upgrade mechanism.
open_items: #462 (Storybook live-upgrade) and release PR #396 still await user approval/merge.
Live upgrade has never been run in a real `storybook dev` browser; multi-tab and timing paths are covered only by tests. napi nextest, `just semver` and a browser run were not re-run.
A closed tab's last component stays tracked since the channel doesn't signal closure (at most one extra request).
Next-stories queue is one per process (last opened tab wins); eager sessions now return checker props, a visible behavior change.
S7 slice feat/fallback-off-rows is running; follow-ups are resolver deletion (S7c-e), quiet-machine Storybook measurement, and the oracle run (user's cost call).
Proposed CLAUDE.md rewording of the fail-on-base rule by change type, and a permanent CI identity golden plus scoped mutation testing, awaiting user's go.
